questions.q: Which spacecraft made the first landing on the far side of the Moon, and when?
questions.do: Press Far side on The landing globe and tap the green dots, or set Decade to 2010s.
questions.a: Chang'e 4 from China, on 3 January 2019, in Von Kármán crater. Because the far side never faces Earth, its messages travel through a relay satellite called Queqiao.

questions.q: How far is it across the Moon's surface from Chandrayaan-3 to Chang'e 6, and which way does the shortest path go?
questions.a: About 2,089 km. The shortest path passes close to the south pole (its furthest point is about 88° S), because the two sites are on opposite sides of the Moon.

questions.q: Which landing is the farthest south anyone has landed, and what went wrong?
questions.do: Press South pole on the globe and tap the gold rings, or find it in Every landing, in order.
questions.a: Athena (IM-2) from Intuitive Machines, at about 84.8° S on 6 March 2025. It ended up on its side in a small, cold, dark crater where its solar panels could not charge, and stopped working the next day.

questions.q: Why does everyone want to land near the Moon's south pole now?
questions.a: Some crater floors there have never seen sunlight and are colder than −200 °C, so they trap water ice. Chandrayaan-1's M3 instrument found signs of water in 2009, and found surface ice in shadowed craters in 2018. Ice could give drinking water, air to breathe and rocket fuel.

questions.q: Which was the first spacecraft ever to land gently on the Moon, and what did it prove?
questions.do: Set Decade to 1960s and tap the first entry in Every landing, in order.
questions.a: The Soviet Union's Luna 9, on 3 February 1966, in the Ocean of Storms. Its photos showed the ground was firm enough to stand on, not deep dust that would swallow a spacecraft.
